text_fidelity_a:
(Old Model) Seagate Backup Plus 2TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STCA2000100) How long are these supposed to last, anyway? I bought mine in late 2012, and subjected it to what I would consider average use. I used it to store movies, videos, and photos. Three days ago (it is now Feb 2015), it started making a weird noise, then stopped working completely. If I powercycle it, it will make the weird noise (like not-so-muffled clicking sounds) for a few seconds and then turn itself off. The computer doesn't recognize it anymore. I even tried plugging it in to a different computer, but it behaved exactly the same way. I KNOW hard drives eventually die, but every other hard drive I've ever had gave some sort of warning that it was dying. Weird noises would start happening, and I would have enough time to buy a new one and move all my data. This one had NO warning and just DIED. Thank goodness I have cloud backup for my photos. My movies are gone, though.

WHILE IT WAS WORKING, it was decent. Quiet and always functional. Not terribly fast on read / write, especially large file transfers inbound and outbound. It never gave me problems, which is why I'm so incredibly annoyed that one day it just decided to not work at all. I don't think I'll ever buy a consumer-grade Seagate product again.
text_fidelity_b: (Old Model) Seagate Backup Plus 2TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STCA2000100)

Three and a half stars.

The output for the USB ports is 5V, 3A Max.

The USB ports glow blue whether you use them or not. The blue light is bright during the day and night, and can be seen even when there is a cable plugged into a port. It picks up 19 stations in the "low country" around a lot of tall pine trees.(20 is the max number of stations in a 60 mile radius here with any antenna according to the TV manufacturer).

You can paint the ant/ cables to match the walls. Comes with push pins for walls and Velcro for wall or window if you want them.Also has a plug into TV for the amp or you can plug into the wall like I did so it isn't hampered by the surge protector.

I get ABC, CBS,NBC,FOX,THIS,3 PBS stations, 3 Christian channels,a Spanish channel, WE,GET,MY,BOUNCE,YOU TOO, one music video channel and one other. The reception on all (but 2) is exceptionally strong with no blips in power even if you cannot put it in a window. I have mine hanging behind my curtain and most channels get 90-100% station strength almost constantly when 35%, even 30% will give you the station clear enough to watch a program with very few "blips" in reception.

I am enjoying not adjusting the Rabbit ear antenna (when I watched certain channels) even though it worked *good* enough for the money.

If you had another antenna before that only picked up 5-13 channels (for exp.) and you switch to a more powerful one like this, remember to unplug your TV a good minute before re- auto programming ( I forgot at first myself) as some TVs seem to "remember" how many it gets and stops at that number.

No need for an ugly outside antenna with this one.

When I use my hair dryer or turn on another "power draw", it doesnt get the interference the previous amplified antenna had, so probably uses less electricity, yet pulls in more stations.
I'm very happy with it. I get more channels than my basic cable had that I enjoy watching also.

Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod, Black The Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod is basically (pardon the pun) everything you need in a monopod. It extends to a nice height and even at full extension it feels reasonably sturdy. Collapsing the thinnest section and using just the two thicker sections increases the stability greatly and still gives you a little over 51 inches to work with.

Build quality is decent. The locking cams are hard plastic but don't feel cheap and give a positive, tight lock when engaged. The foam grip isn't glued into place. It is just held in place by friction and the three screw heads that hold the camera mount to the monopod.

The monopod also includes a wrist strap held in place on the head of the mount by a split ring.

A carry bag is supplied. It's enough to protect the monopod though it's not padded and the shoulder strap is short enough to be more of a carry strap.

The rubber foot of this monopod can be retracted on its threaded mount to expose a metal spike foot for use in outdoor.

The only negatives I've found with this monopod are:
The wrist strap is rather small and I cannot fit it over my hand. For reference I wear a size large glove. For me this is more of a palm strap.

The soft foot has very little rubber extending past the end of the metal spike. I measured this at just slightly over 1mm. Moderate wear will surely leave the metal foot expose and potentially damage flooring.

All in all though this is an affordable and well built monopod and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics 67-Inch Monopod, Black

Canon PowerShot ELPH 520 HS 10.1 MP CMOS Digital Camera with 12x Ultra Wide-Angle Optical Image Stabilized Zoom Lens and Full 1080p HD Video (Blue) I'm really happy with this camera. It takes great snapshots, and it is so small that I can always have it with me. Nobody will ever mistake it for a several thousand dollar DSLR, either in price, weight, or picture quality, but the 12x zoom in such a small package was the sweet spot for me. And lets face it, for most of us, being able to get the shot because you have your camera is much more important than the really high quality picture--that you're never going to blow up to room size anyway--that you would have got if only you hadn't left your big, heavy, awkward DSLR at home!

Some folks have compared the quality to cell phones. There's no comparison. I can get shots that are just dark blobs on the iPhone. The battery is pretty small, though, so make sure you have two or three, which I have always done anyway (they're small, so it isn't that big a deal). Be careful if you buy an off brand battery: Many of them have LESS capacity. Don't go by the picture, many of them appear to be photoshopped to say 1000mAH, but the specs give you the real value. I picked up the [[ASIN:B004M640YU Wasabi Power Battery for Canon NB-9L and Canon PowerShot SD4500 IS, ELPH 510 HS, ELPH 520 HS, ELPH 530 HS]], and it seems OK so far, but I haven't rigorously tested it. Sony ICFC218 Dream Machine Clock Radio (Black) This is not a bad clock radio for the price I paid. It's not a great one either, but it fit the profile of what I wanted with one exception, which I'll get to in a bit.

First off, it's smallish, which is a blessing on a crowded nightstand. The display seems fine to me, neither too bright, nor too dim. It's easy to program, thank goodness. I've had a lot of electronics that require three hands, and a stopwatch to be properly programmed. The ICF-C218 has a button or a dial for each function. Just follow the instructions and you'll be fine. It's a bit hard to see the radio dial unless you pick it up, but that's a minor thing for someone like me, who pretty much keeps it on one station. It's not programmable; you have to change the station with a tuning dial. However the reception is excellent, even without an external antenna.

My quibble, and it's a relatively small one, is that the sound is tinny. I don't expect a lot out of a small radio like this, but I have a Sangean which is even smaller, and the sound is much better. It's not a deal-breaker, I got what I wanted in every other respect.

Bottom line: Good price point for a basic clock radio with excellent reception, and so-so sound.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFC218 Dream Machine Clock Radio (Black)

Targus Vuscape Case and Stand for iPad mini (fits iPad mini 1, 2, 3) Black (THZ182US) The Targus VuScape Protective cover and stand is a pretty good, helpful aid for those who own an Apple Ipad2. It features a thin, lightweight design that is meant to hold the iPad2 snugly in place while you work.

Having a stand for your iPad is certainly a good idea and I like that this stand can be used to position your iPad in different ways. There are multiple grooves so that you can display your iPad at different angles. The cover can also be folded back completely, allowing the consumer to hold the iPad in the hands without the stand.

This protective cover/stand does have some nice features to offer, but after using it for a while, it is more than apparent that the stand is not perfect. Probably the greatest issue is that the stand isn't as sturdy as I would prefer. If you use the stand on a solid, flat surface, you shouldn't have too many problems, but place it on other surfaces and it tends to bend just a little bit. The slightest bend will cause the grooves to give way just a little, and the iPad will no longer be securely held in place.

I generally like the thin, lightweight design of this stand, but the thinness possibly goes a tad far. If the manufacturer had made this stand just a little bit thicker, it would be stronger and more likely to hold the iPad in place without any problems. I suppose this is the trade- off one must make when selecting a stand such as this. Lightweight is nice, especially for something like an iPad, but lightweight means the stand is lacking in strength.

All in all, this is a good stand and certainly worth considering, but not a deluxe stand like I expected. Again, as long as you are willing to sacrifice sturdiness for lightweight design, you should be fine. And try to use only on the flattest surfaces for the best results. Follow these guidelines and you should find yourself reasonably happy with this protective cover and stand from Targus.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Vuscape Case and Stand for iPad mini (fits iPad mini 1, 2, 3) Black (THZ182US)

One day it just stopped charging. I had read dozens of books on there, and had the wifi plus 3g version which was very convenient.

I occasionally read now on the Kindle app on my computer, as I have about 97 books in my library, with probably 15-20 still unread. I noticed on Amazon that there was a promotion...Kindles on sale for Prime members. Also, some of the reviews of the higher end Kindles did not impress me.

Anyway, I received the Kindle earlier today. It came almost fully charged, and was so easy to set up. And within minutes had books from my Kindle library loaded! I am using it on maximum brightness, sure it may take more frequent charging, but I really love how bright it is and the contrast of the words on the page. I also bought a cover for it and find it is easier to hold IMO. Pages turned with a simple finger swipe.

Hopefully this will last a very long time! I've got so many books I want to read!

text_fidelity_a:
TREBLAB Z2 | Over Ear Workout Headphones with Microphone | Bluetooth 5.0, Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) | Up to 35H Battery Life | Wireless Headphones for Sport, Workout, Running, Gym I wanted to find a cheaper alternative to my wife's wireless Bose headset, something with decent noise cancelling for flights and work. So far I've used Bose, the MPOW H5, Treblab, and Woltix with ANC.

The sound on these are first class - really great highs, mids, and lows - tons of clarity (when active noise cancel is on...otherwise it sounds a bit muggy). Very comfortable and light. BUT - I got these because they are wireless with active noise cancellation, and although the ANC is effective, if you are in a quiet room you'll hear a slight hiss when the ANC is on - many people report the same thing in reviews, and it's true - you'll hear it. You won't notice this when music is on or during a flight. I often use these at coffee shops just to zone out and focus on work, and I could notice the slight hiss in quieter environments.

I've also used Bose, the MPOW H5, and Woltix with ANC. I didn't want to buy another Bose headset when my wife and I travel together. Nothing will compare to Bose noise cancellation, but the MPOW H5 and Woltix are actually really nice for the money. The MPOW H5 don't have as good audio clarity as the Treblab, but at the end of the day I got noise cancelling headphones for the noise canceling. I ended up returning the Treblab and the MPOW H5 and I kept the Woltix because they are more comfortable than the MPOW and had the best low-price ANC. The MPOW also had some sound interference issues randomly when the ANC was on.

So:

Bose: Best noise cancellation, good audio, comfortable, but definitely expensive!
Treblab: Best audio, worst noise cancellation (you can hear a slight hiss when turned on), comfortable, but large and they don't fold down too small.
MPOW: Good audio, good noise cancellation, but was getting some weird sound interference with the ANC on sometimes. Tight on ears.
Woltix: Good audio, good noise cancellation, most comfortable (way lighter and less tight on the ears than the MPOW), and fold down the smallest.
text_fidelity_b: TREBLAB Z2 | Over Ear Workout Headphones with Microphone | Bluetooth 5.0, Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) | Up to 35H Battery Life | Wireless Headphones for Sport, Workout, Running, Gym

Cambridge Soundworks OontZ Angle 3XL Ultra Bluetooth Speaker - Portable Bluetooth Speakers I found it 'dark' and muffled at first. After putting an equalizer in front of it (I used the Windows 7 Equalizer APO 1.2.1, which has it's own graphic equalizer to play around with, and is free), I could tweak the response so that the speaker sounds very high fidelity and even across the frequency range. I am including a screengrab of the equalizer settings I use. As you can see it just needs a bit of tweaking to make it sound it's best. The volume is more than sufficient, but you need to put the speaker volume up high and adjust the volume from your computer or phone. Otherwise, there is a tendency to putting the volume up too high on the phone or computer and over driving the speaker, which will make it sound really distorted.

I spent half the day playing it at roughly 1/3 volume without it running out of power. I take it with me to work, and out on the porch. It's very versatile, but bigger and heavier than most bluetooth portable speakers. It's the price you pay for deep bass, and high quality drivers. If sound is most important to you, go with this. They can also be paired, which must sound very very good indeed.

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation Another reviewer mentioned these issues, but I was impulsive and bought it anyways. They are all true.
- I spend a good deal of time adjusting the sensibility settings and using the brackets (both V and H) to reduce false positives, but they are still too many. My door is about 25-30' from the road and if a truck passes, even small cars, "motion detected". You stop giving importance for the sensor.
- I try to answer motion but it takes so long to load (I have an S8, with good wifi) and I got a connection problem way too often. If wasn't another false positive (as usually is), I would have missed the person lurking.
- The recording starts too late. when you go see the recorded video (because you were not able to answer the false positive motion), the video starts way too long after the movement started.
- regarding payments: I have a Piper camera that records up to 1,000 24s videos for free, overwriting after that. It works great. It always worked. Why Ring enforce additional payment is mind-blowing considering what is available on the market.
- I have installed with battery, that was really good because it was easy to install, but on the current pace (75% after 25 days) there is no way it will last the suggested 6 months on the website.

UPDATE: had to completely disable the motion sensor, the false positives were driving me crazy. Not paying the monthly fee. It's too many clicks to get to the screen when somebody actually pushes the button.
Avoid this product and wait for competitors to come up with something better.
UPDATE 2: Now this piece of crap will not enter live view.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Video Doorbell 2 with HD Video, Motion Activated Alerts, Easy Installation

SAFEMORE USB Power Strip 8-Outlet and 4 USB Charging Ports with 6.5-Feet Cord (Pure Black) I have a workbench where I frequently have little projects underway, and the issue I have had is a shortage of power outlets so I am frequently changing the configuration on my desk to account for this. I decided to use this surge suppressor/power strip on my workbench to resolve this issue and so far it has worked out well for me.

There are eight full-sized, grounded power outlets on this tower, and each one is spaced properly to handle a full-sized power adapter like what comes with many electronics. As such, there is no need to compromise when plugging in devices that have larger adapters, because there is enough room for all on this tower. Every outlet includes a ground plug too, which is great for devices that require one (in my house, it's about 50/50). With almost every other surge suppressor, I have had issues with oversized adapters crowding other outlets – this is not a problem with this one.

There are also four USB charging ports on this tower which is a really nice bonus. These are all 2.1A ports so they can output a full-speed charge to devices that can handle it, but most of my devices take a 1A charge so the 2.1A is lost on me. I have not yet put a meter on these ports to check the actual power output but so far these seem to output about the same as most other USB charging blocks I have used. Power output aside, having USB and AC ports together allows choice if you have a device that uses a USB adapter to plug into an AC outlet.

The circuit breaker button is on the bottom.

One thing I particularly like about this tower is that the outlets are one two circuits and there are buttons (on the top) that control each circuit. This may require a little logic when planning your power usage – if you want only/all lights on one circuit, place them so that they are controlled by a single button and you can then power them all on and off together.

This tower have allowed me to clean up my work area and it has enough outlets on it to cover my devices without issue. It is very easy to use and understand, it has plenty of outlets that are spaced apart nicely so there is no waste, and it includes USB outlets too. I have had no trouble with it at all and have no problem recommending it it if you are looking for a good power strip/surge suppressor.

Disclosure: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no/minimal cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: SAFEMORE USB Power Strip 8-Outlet and 4 USB Charging Ports with 6.5-Feet Cord (Pure Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black As an avid fan of Alexa, I am delighted to have this Harman Kardon Alexa speaker. I've had my original Echo since the first week they released the initial invitation to buy and have since added a Dot and Alexa controlled thermostats, dining room lights, Fire TV sticks and plugs through out the house. This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.
text_fidelity_b: Harman Kardon Allure Voice-Activated Home Speaker with Alexa, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black First a caveat: I am not of the generation who grew up carrying backpacks to school and I do not have a lot of shoulder/upper arm strength; in addition I have arthritis in my neck, so to me any backpack seems a bit strange, stiff, and awkward. Frankly, I think if I'd had to carry around all the books I did in junior high school in a backpack (none of my classes were near my homeroom locker, so there was none of this dropping books off routine--we only had three minutes to get between classes), I'd have severe back problems right now, remembering the thick English, math, science, Italian, and history textbooks, plus a full size ring binder. Oy.

Now to our backpack: I like this. We have less expensive backpacks in our home, to use as a "bug out" bag in case of emergency. This is much nicer: padding, quality of material, and lots of nice pockets (I am a pockets-type person). I particularly like the "hidden pocket" that faces your back, which would be useful for money or any other valuables if you were backpacking or traveling. I have preliminarily tested this by putting my laptop and my 10-inch tablet in the space provided and walking around for a bit. My laptop is six years old and weighs a ton. However, the padded shoulder straps and the sternum strap were helpful in keeping this balanced well on my back. I went up and down stairs a few times and did not feel unbalanced or "top heavy." (I do now, however, understand why people like Airbooks.)

In addition to the laptop pocket with the inner sleeve for the tablet, this has a central compartment with two pockets, one zipped, and an outside compartment with all sorts of slots for pens, memory cards, CDs, whatever. A small pocket on the top of the back could hold a cell phone or perhaps your printout of a boarding pass, parking ticket receipt, whatever, and there are two small pockets, one on each side, one with an opening so you could put an .mp3 player in the pocket and have your earbuds come out through it. This is all in addition to the "hidden pocket." There is a strong handle at either end of the backpack as well as a handle.

My goal is to give this a better workout at Dragoncon, where I can carry lunch and snacks and juice boxes in the central compartment, carry my tablet in the laptop compartment, and also carry my camera, instead of slinging a lunchbox and my camera case over my shoulder. It seems like a much better option. I also see it being useful on the occasional weekend trip. If it works out for me, it's possible my husband might enjoy one as well.

[September: This was really, really good at Dragoncon; I will be using a backpack again next year. Much better than carrying the lunchbox and the camera separately and wearing a pouch. I put my tablet in the laptop pocket, my lunch things (juice boxes, sandwiches, snacks, fruit) in the middle pocket, and the camera in the outermost pocket. The little pocket at the top held my spare cell phone batteries, and my wallet was in the hidden pocket. This backpack needs a strap at the bottom, and, instead of an iPod holder, a water bottle holder. That's the only thing I can see wrong with it. Yeah, I could have put a water bottle inside with my lunch.]

[PS I liked this so much I bought my husband one for Christmas.]
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung 860 QVO SSD 4TB - 2.5 Inch SATA 3 Internal Solid State Drive with V-NAND Technology (MZ-76Q4T0B/AM), Gray I’ve had this SSD for a few days and I also have a 1TB 970 Evo Plus and 1TB 860 Evo and all of them are great! But they do have their drawbacks too.

This drive does really well with SMALL (under 15Gb) workloads. The speeds are right up there (~500MB/s R/W) with my 860 Evo until it gets to about ~14GB at which point it slows down drastically. This is fine for things like boot, games, apps, and most programs.

However, if you do heavy workloads like video editing, file transfers, etc,. where you are regularly moving large (15GB+) files around this is NOT the drive for you. If you are a “heavy” user I highly recommend the 860 Pro. It can keep up those high R/W speeds without slowing down after ~15GB. It will maintain full speed throughout the duration of whatever you are doing.

With that said this is a great drive for light/moderate workloads (gaming, web browsing, small work files, etc.,) and it is at a price that gives you excellent value and quality for your money.

I also really love the Samsung Magician software. It’s basically the main reason why 3/5 of my drives are Samsung. Samsung is also known for making reliable, high quality products. Yes there is a premium compared to cheaper drives but you’re paying that little bit extra for quality & reliability.

I took off 1 Star on this review though because Samsung doesn’t include any of the cables or mounting screws which just doesn’t make sense to me. C’mon Samsung start adding that stuff! I would’ve happily paid a couple dollars more for it and it wouldn’t have cost Samsung that much so they could’ve made a little bit of extra profit by adding it.

I still recommend this drive though and would buy it or the 860 Evo again if I needed more storage.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 860 QVO SSD 4TB - 2.5 Inch SATA 3 Internal Solid State Drive with V-NAND Technology (MZ-76Q4T0B/AM), Gray

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black I don't know what to think of these headphones. The sound out of the box is terrible, just abysmal. I've never heard a more unbalanced headphone anywhere. If you can't use an eq with these headphones, stop reading and look elsewhere.

If you can use an eq in your application, you might find these headphones surprising. Once the shrill high-end is toned down and the bass and mids bumped up, you will find the sound is pretty good for a ~$60/pair. The soundstage is small, but clear and the instrument separation surpasses what I was expecting. However, boost the bass too much and you will get distortion.

A couple of weeks before buying these I heard the quad-driver version and they were simply amazing. It was like I was sitting in my own living room listening to a full surround sound setup. I've never heard spacial definition or as big a soundstage in a headphone as I did with the quad-drivers, especially IEMs. The quad-drivers are on par with $600/pair HiFiMan planars. That's why I took a chance on this much cheaper bluetooth version of a single driver.

If you don't mind playing with the eq and don't want to buy cheap knock-offs from china (these are made in china, but by the company that designed them), take a chance on these. If you just want to plug and play, buy something else. I'm still on the fence on returning them myself.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

This came in a box. It has basic information in it.

CORD
The cord is actually 6.6 ft long. I needed the extra length for the place I had set aside for it.

LAYOUT
The layout of this outlet strip is excellent I can put any type of plug in there and it works. The USB cords are also laid out well.

I use this as a wall mount to plug in my aquarium pumps, lights, etc. into. The small footprint makes it great to use.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice compact little outlet strip/box. It is set up well and works well. It does have a light on it, though, so if planning to use in a bedroom keep that in mind.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great unit. I am going to get this when my UPS units finally fail in my sewing room so that I can have a small outlet to use out of the way instead of the big UPS one that has given me issues anyway.

TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9) Gigabit ports for plugged devices maximize my cable connection. I have 100Mbs rated Internet. Old netgear router with 100Mb ports would only get 72Mbs speed tests. This Archer 9 gets me 112Mbs throughput on wired connections. I also love the ability to have two radios at 2.4 and 5ghz. I named both of my SSIDs the same, and the router and devices are smart enough to pick the fastest and most efficient radio. Devices like my WiFi printer selected the 2.4ghz, while my apple devices all go on the 5gjz spectrum. The smartphone app is nice to use and is easy to setup the router with basic functionality. You’ll need the browser though if you wish to fine tune settings for the more IT type folks like myself. The app allows you a quick glance to see what/how many devices are connected, and you can easily kick a device off if you choose to.
Overall, I am quite pleased with this Archer AC1900. It performs automatic firmware updates for the latest security patches if needed as well. Aesthetically, it is also pretty cool looking, and not just a square black box. I also like that is stands vertically, so it has a smaller footprint while actually increasing radio coverage.
Overall, I would recommend this router, and it is slightly less expensive than other comparable brands.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1900 Smart Wireless Router - Beamforming Dual Band Gigabit WiFi Internet Routers for Home, High Speed, Long Range, Ideal for Gaming (Archer C9)

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS N53SM-ES72 15.6-Inch Laptop (Silver Aluminum) I'll update later. First thing I did was toy with it a little to make sure it worked, then I installed Ubuntu 12.04. THEN I found out that there are not reliable drivers for using the optimus feature in linux. I went with this laptop so that I can play one game in particular. After spending HOURS tweeking, installing and experimenting, I'm at the point where I can say, if you plan on using this machine for linux AND gaming, either walk on by, or plan on dual booting or running a virtual machine (which one I've not decided I'll do yet). I THINK if there was the ability in the BIOS to turn off the intel graphics card in favor of only using the nvidia, that might be helpful.
The design is nice, it's fast and it may be heavy by today's standards, but compared to the Dell d810 I'm replacing, this is light.
The price point is, as stated by many before, excellent.

I take away the star for the simple fact that it's FAR too late in the game for nvidia to not have appropriate drivers to support this card fully in linux.

I do NOT want to run windows 7, but it looks like I'll be recovering it and spending hours decrapifying.

Update: May, 14, 2012
I've now had the laptop running a dual boot of Ubuntu 12.04 and Windows 7. I initially tried to just run Ubuntu and gave up on the driver debacle - fail for nvidia - and went back to reinstall. Major advice, when you get this machine, BOOT IT AND MAKE THE RECOVERY DVD SET!!! It took 4 DVDs and actually a little while, but it was the best move. When I went to recover W7, it did not properly use the recovery partition. The DVDs rebuild the partition (and destroy everything else in the process) back to factory. That was ok for me, I was testing and didn't lose anything worth saving.

Boot is fast. Ubuntu shuts down super fast, so the time to switch isn't bad. I play my game (Lord of the Rings Online - mostly set as ultra settings) quit and reboot into linux so I can enjoy my daily computing experience.

The plus other mention is the full HD experience. My previous laptop did 1900x100. I miss the vertical resolution, but am getting used to only having 1080. The screen is great. I do not understand why people like the glossy/glare screens. I hate them. This is pretty matte.

Temperature-wise it runs lap-top ok. The left side vent blows warm/hot air, which was actually nice on my hand in the cold basement during gaming (I'm a lefty - using a mouse).

I'm getting used to the keyboard. I often find it misses some of my key strokes, but I might just need to MEAN them a little more, as I tend to type with a softer touch. This makes the typing experience a little louder than I prefer, but my wife doesn't complain, so it can't be that bad.

I'm a tad less fond of the USB placement. They are toward the front of the sides, which means the USB plugs are close to all my business. If I had the RJ45 connected as well, it would be more annoying wires up close and personal.

As or resources, it feels perfectly adequate for my needs. This weekend I was running about 60 firefox tabs, 10 chrome tabs, a handful of libre office documents, Redblade 3.5 (D&D character generator) running twice via wine, about 15 20-50MB PDFs, ktorrent, and a few other things here and there concurrently without a hiccup. Eventually, maybe I'll upgrade to more ram, but I cannot currently see any reason for it. I also can't see a particular reason to plunk down for a SSD. I imagine the power saving would be nice. I do get only around 2-2.5 hours of regular use off power, but since this is a desktop replacement, that's less of an issue. If it was less than 1.5 hrs, I'd be troubled.

The quickboot option boots into an OS experience for basic web browsing, some games, IM... I suppose the most basic of what a netbook would be for. In a pinch, it's FAST to get into and connects to wifi quickly. Navigating is funky, but it's not meant for full on use - otherwise you blew $900 on a pretty low end experience.

I still deduct the star almost exclusively for the video drivers issue and the inability to select which video to use in the BIOS. If I could run from the nvidia, I believe there wouldn't be the issues with driver support in linux, as the GPU is supported - it's the switching that's picky.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS N53SM-ES72 15.6-Inch Laptop (Silver Aluminum)

text_fidelity_a:
FAVI FE01 2.4GHz Wireless USB Mini Keyboard with Mouse Touchpad, Laser Pointer - USA Version (Warranty) - Black (FE01-BL) There are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews of this keyboard, so I will stick to how I am using the review sample that I received, and a few of my impressions.

First, this is not a bluetooth device (it was described as such to me when I was asked to review it.) The only weak point is the documentation, which is terse, but well illustrated. Had it contained specs and compatibility data it would have been significantly more useful. However, this is not a major flaw.

I first tested it with an ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. It was immediately recognized and functional. My next test was to see if it would work with my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone running Android 4.4.2. I connected with wireless dongle via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]] and it worked. To be honest, that arrangement is a bit on the clumsy side for me.

My final test and where this keyboard shines is when I connected it to my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 Smart TV BOX]] running Android 4.2. This keyboard made a lot of sense connected to that box because I rarely used it prior. I was using a corded keyboard and it was a trip hazard. Plus most of in interaction with it included few keystrokes, so this mini keyboard is perfect. In fact I find myself using the TV box a lot more frequently now that I have this keyboard. I think of it as a smart remote control - which it is - and have quickly grown to love it.

As for prolonged typing, this would not be my favorite solution. However, that is subjective. I hated my Blackerry when I was required to carry one back in my consulting days too. But for occasional use this is wonderful.

Bottom line: I would have never guessed that this would be the missing link between me and my TV box. Had I only tested this with phones and tablets I would have probably written a single word review: meh. Now, though, I see the wow factor.
text_fidelity_b: FAVI FE01 2.4GHz Wireless USB Mini Keyboard with Mouse Touchpad, Laser Pointer - USA Version (Warranty) - Black (FE01-BL)

AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+ FD4100WMGUSBX My old computer was exactly that: Old! It needed some serious work. I was running an Athlon X2 6000+ and an EVGA 9800GT. It was a great system back in the day! But, time took its toll. I was kicking around the idea of getting an Intel i3, since they seem to edge out this chip, and are competitively priced (I never overclock my equipment, so it's at stock settings.) But the future upgradability seemed like it'd be very costly. Over all, this chip performs just fine. I mainly upgraded so I could play Diablo 3, and with an EVGA 550 Ti, I play it on high settings, and it looks as good as I could want it to look. My old machine did just fine with standard productivity stuff, but I wanted to play games that were more recent than WoW. I'm able to do everything I want, with no signs of a lag. If I need to upgrade, I'm banking that the next generation of this chip will see some improvements (though the improvement I'm seeing from my last CPU is leaps-and bounds!) The AM3+ socket will be around for a while. Over all, this is a great chip, and easy on the wallet.

**Update 9/6/12**
I recently purchased Guild Wars 2. The game is fairly CPU-intensive, but the FX-4100 keeps up just fine! I think I'm sitting at around 50% plus load at any given time during actual game play on all four cores. I haven't had a single hiccup or spot of lag yet!

Starcraft 2 is another CPU-heavy application, and coupled with the 550 Ti card, I'm running it on Extreme at 1400x900 resolution, and it's flawless. Again, all four cores are loaded, and quite frequently, they're over 60%. Things get a little warm (35C or so) when compared to when I run other applications. Nothing to worry about!

I have also paid quite a bit of attention to how it runs with Diablo 3. It only uses 2 cores at about 50% load at any given time. That game is more GPU-intensive. I am still very happy with my purchase!
text_fidelity_b: AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+  FD4100WMGUSBX

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black Do not buy this if you're looking for the fastest tablet. That's not what it is, though it's by no means slow. It will take a lot more abuse than the fastest tablets available for the same price. You can stand outside in the rain or snow and use the touchscreen when it's wet. You can drop it in the mud, pick it up, wipe it off, and keep using it. I wouldn't take it scuba diving though. I will take it off-roading. This one has enough storage to preload maps for off-road hiking/biking/riding/driving for when there's no signal at all.

I've seen several questions about whether this works with Verizon, and several people answer that it doesn't. Those people are wrong. The Enterprise/LTE/4G/WiFi version does work with Verizon. It should work with others. Find this model number (SM-T577UZKGN14) on the Samsung site to check. Samsung knows. Those other people don't.

This is the third tablet I've used my Verizon SIM card in. The first was a tablet I bought through Verizon. The second was a TabActive2, and now I'm using the same SIM card in this TabActive3. This does not apply to the WiFi-only version. Don't confuse the two.

I pulled the SIM card out of the TabActive2, inserted it in the TabActive3, restarted the device as requested, and a few minutes later the line was active on the new device. I ignored Verizon's emailed instructions, because they don't appear to apply to swapping a current SIM card into a new device. I even restored a Google backup from the 2 to the 3 and saved a lot of time installing apps.

So, why this tablet? It's rugged. It's Samsung. I really like having an 8" tablet. It works with Verizon.

Why 4G/LTE? It's not 5G. I drive a truck through at least 5 states on a regular basis, and in some areas the signal constantly switches between 4G and 5G and the data connection is interrupted. When I can't access online banking, credit cards, and apps relating to business with my 5G phone, I often can with a 4G tablet. I have unlimited data on a second plan for only $10/mth, since I already have a smartphone plan. No hotspot/WiFi needed.

Why upgrade? My TabActive2 only had 16GB of internal storage. The TabActive3 I bought has 128GB. The TabActive3 has DEX. The TabActive2 didn't. I didn't manage to hurt the 2, and the 3 is physically very similar. The 3 has a faster CPU, and a faster GPU.

From the beginning, everything about the TabActive2 as a usable tablet simply wasn't enough. It wasn't fast enough. It didn't have enough storage. But it was rugged. It still is. This is the first time I've upgraded when the old tablet still worked as well as it did when I bought it. It appears that the TabActive3 is just as rugged.

Con: The biggest downside to these is that there's no external charger that I can find for the replaceable battery. At least I can't find one. Maybe one exists. I have no evidence of that. It is possible to buy another compatible battery, but I can't find any way to charge said battery other than to charge it in the tablet, and it's a pain to get to, because of the lengths Samsung went to to seal the battery compartment. The battery life is substantial, partly due to the less-than-premium performance, but it would really be nice to be able to easily carry a fully-charged spare.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Nuforce NE-700X Titanium Coated In-Ear Headphones - Aqua Silver Update after a couple of months

I still love 'em. Everything I put below still holds true. I rarely touch the EQ, and have been able to return to less processing is good processing listening.

One thing to add is that these are the first earbuds I could lay on my side with my head on the pillow and be comfortable. They have minimal strain relief but so far the cords have been perfect. I'd call tangle factor about medium.

++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Original review

So far I've tried
Skull Candy Titan - For me the best bass sound in this bunch. Tight punchy, accentuated but enjoyably so. Good for working out. But I value accurate bass above all. So I just use these for working out now.
Vsonic GR99 - very nice balanced sounding for $20ish dollars
Vsonic VC02 - Great sounding, but not a lot of bass. But what bass that was there was VERY good. My favorite phones in this list. But I kept losing the ear piece because of the removable wires. After the 2nd time I moved onto the VSD1
Vsonic VSD1 - nice sounding, if somewhat dry. It didn't make me get into my music, and I couldn't get them comfortable in my ears
Brainwaves S1 - These were my least favorite, boomy and not very comfortable, heavy thick wires. The only pair of the above I returned.

What they do well - assume anything not here is more than adequate

Presentation - I feel like I'm getting what the engineer was going for in the mix. More musical than any of the above without falling into a 'warm sound'. A nice mix of forgiving and accurate. Brightness right about where it should be.
Sound Stage - Airy, instruments well placed. Center image is not the strongest, but not lacking. Does a nice job of presenting the room acoustics/reverb in the mix.
Drums - Drums are rendered very well, better than any of the the above.
Cymbals - rendered very well, especially high hat. You can tell the cymbals are made of metal, and not just the tik-tik of the drum stick tip
Treble-sibilance - Close to perfect. Nice and bright without getting into hissy/tizzy. Vocal articulation is good.
Very easy to listen to for long periods of time. They are accurate without being piercing or harsh.
Sounded good right out of the box.

Misc sound notes - distorted electric guitar is just right. They respond to EQ very well, (which the Brainwavz did not do). I really notice when something comes into the mix even if it is soft. And louder things like guitar solos, really punch in the way you hear when mixing in the studio.

If I HAD to critique the sound (this is a review) there is a very-very, (did I mention very?) lack of something in the mids. Think chest/throat area of male vocals. But this is in the realm of sound signature, a matter of taste, not a deficiency and in no way lowers my enjoyment of these.

Build - wires are thin and flexible which is what I wanted. Very nice for wearing over the ear. Microphonics close to none whether worn up or down. No hearing foot steps or wire rubbing/bouncing on clothes. Light cord/cinch is great for running.
Shape - Bullet shaped what can I say, they are light and comfortable. I like the ring of rubber around them. It gives a little grip for inserting/removing them.
I LOVE that they have a red strain relief on the right side. No having to get my glasses to see some tiny R or L printed somewhere. Cord is nice and long, which is nice for using on a treadmill or elliptical trainer, or for wearing the cord under your shirt or down in a pocket.

As much as I liked the over all presentation and frequency response I feel I should point out these are not hella flat-accurate phones (like the VC02). If a true hi-fi sound, bright/accurate/revealing, is what you are after I'd look elsewhere (maybe the VC02) Don't get me wrong, since I used to be a sound engineer, and work on electric guitars, and have very accurate/bright/revealing/fatiguing speakers on my desk, I'm very picky about good accurate sound. But that makes these musical, easy to listen to for very long periods of time and poorly recorded and/or lower quality rips won't be hard to listen to.

The title says it all - the best I've tried yet and the first phones that made me stop 'shopping' for my next pair of phones.

Listening setup. Listening has been through an amp and separate dac connected to my computer playing 192kb - 320k - FLAC music, and through my old Droid Charge (I use this because I can enable the onboard DAC) and my Samsung Note II listening to ripped music (192k or better) or Spotify/Pandora at their highest quality settings available in the premium versions.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer C720 Chromebook (11.6-Inch, 2GB) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** These are pretty much the perfect laptop for kids (and adults too if they don't want to download or install any personal programs). The Google App store has just about every type of app/program you could want. These don't have a DVD drive and you can't download programs unless they are from the App store. It's a good way of keeping your machine safe from malware attacks. No need to purchase and renew antiviral software. The screen is clear and bright, and the keyboard works really nicely. The sound from these is much better than the sound on my much more expensive laptop. Overall, the size and functionality of the Chromebook is much better than my new Windows 8.1 laptop.

My kids were able to get started immediately with minimal help from me to download some apps they like, get their e-mails set up and started using these Chromebooks immediately. I personally am not nuts about having only Google Chrome as my internet browser, thus I don't own my own Chromebook, but for my kids purposes (mainly games and schoolwork) the Chromebooks work out great. I really like how easy and smoothly they work. They are faster than my laptop and I do find that appealing, but I like being able to use a DVD drive and to be able to download what software I might want from the internet.

Printing is possible from the cloud and set up to do that is not difficult. Everything is easy........almost too easy. You can't store any data on the computer itself, only in the cloud. But, I'm not worried about any personal information being accessed by nefarious types because there's really nothing to access.

We've had these Chromebooks since Christmas and they are still working fine with no problems whatsoever.

UPDATE: 2.28.15 - My daughter brought it to my attention that these chromebooks do not have a "delete" key. Interesting.
text_fidelity_b: Acer C720 Chromebook (11.6-Inch, 2GB) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black Finally seem to have found a pair of bluetooth headphones with acceptable connection performance. I was begining to think that it was too much to ask to be able to put my phone in my pocket and still be connected. Or to walk more than a few feet away from my phone and still stay connected. These ace those tests. Connectivity is not perfect but I am willing to accept that as it's bluetooth. I do get the occasional drop for no apparent reason but it is not often enough to be a huge negative.
They come packaged really nicely. So nicely you almost feel obligated to go slow and enjoy the experience.
You have to chose between the silicone or foam ear bud tips. The silicone feels softer and goes in and out easier. The foam will give you a more secure fit and sound isolation. I went with the foam and they do a fairly good job of keeping the outside world out. They are by no means 100 percent effective though.
I used the medium foam tips as well as the ear wings and find the comfort pretty good and the fit very secure. Wearing them for a couple hours was not an issue and I had no discomfort.
I cannot comment on their ability to transmit music as I use them for podcasts. Sound quality was fine for speech.
These have come down in price so much lately that I think they are a no brainer compared to the competition.
I dropped them a star due to the occasional random connection failure but overall I am very pleased with them.
text_fidelity_b: Jaybird X2 Sport Wireless Bluetooth Headphones - Midnight Black

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black We blow through ear buds in our house and it seems that everyone has different ones that they like and don't like. Let's see how these measure up:

WHAT ARE THESE EAR BUDS LIKE?
These ear buds come in a nice box with a little instruction booklet. There is a little bag with three sets of gel caps in it. There are also three sets of hooks. Each of them comes in small medium and large. The hooks keep the buds in the ear but are soft so they don't hurt the ear at all.

The controls are on the right ear- the top hits about where the chin is. The connecting cord is big enough to be worn in front or back. The set comes with a cord but you have to have your own USB access to plug it into whether it be on an outlet or computer.

COMFORT
One of the most comfortable and secure earbud/headsets we have used to date- love that the hooks that help hold them in are soft so they don't hurt the ear, even after worn for a while.

PERFORMANCE
VOLUME
The headset gets the best result for us with the volume on max on the headset and halfway on the tablet that we use it with.

HIGHS/LOWS/MIDS
One of the things with this headset is that the highs are really nice and strong and so are the lows. The problem seems to be that the mids are drowned out making it feel like it is a bit out of balance. We have messed with it quite a bit and it seems to be the way it is.

SOUND PROOFING
These have excellent sound insulation capabilities. That does mean, however, that you need to be careful where you are wearing them if you need to hear what is around you or not.

BATTERY ALERT
When you first turn on the headphones, it will identify itself, tell you it is pairing and then give you an idea of how much battery life you have left- low, medium, or high.

POWER BUTTON
The power button is nice. Volume/skip functions are a challenge to get used to as compared to other Bluetooth headsets. There are sequences and timing as compared to others which seem to be simpler to use.

PAIRING
Very good pairing on all of the different devices we tested this with- several phones from Moto G3, Blu phone, Samsung Tablets and our stereo (forgot brand)

CHARGE
A charge has been lasting a good six to eight hours for us. Recharging seems to take us about three hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These are comfortable headphones that are easy to use, stay in the ears well, and have good insulation from ambient noise in the room or surroundings. They have nice highs and lows but tend to drown out the mids. The controls are a bit more challenging to learn at first as compared to other Bluetooth head sets we have used.

MY RATING
FOUR AND A HALF STARS- not able to give that so I am doing four. It is more like four and a half. The sound could be a little more balanced, and the controls not quite so difficult, but this is still a great set of headphones and we like it a lot.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE iBFree In-Ear Earphones Wireless Headphones with Bluetooth 4.2 AAC, IPX 6 Waterproof, Secure Fit, In-Line Mic for Sports Gym Running - New Model Black

Logitech Wireless Headset for iPad, iPhone and iPod Touch The positives about these headphones outnumber the negatives.

In no particular order;

1. Easy set up. Like all bluetooth devices, these headphones were a quick set up by simply turning them on and my mac responded with 'Do You Want To Use This Device?' The total set up time, approximately sixty seconds!

2.Excellent for VOIP gmail phone.

3. You can charge the headset, while you are using it. So on marathon conference call days, I can plug them in, while using them for about twenty minutes and then they are charged enough to last through a long, boring, three hour conference call (more's the pity!).

4. They charge off the USB port and they come with a cable for doing this.

5. They are lightweight and comfortable to wear, so no headaches!

6. Adjustable volume which is perfect for the hard of hearing.

The negatives, in no particular order;

1. The sound quality is not so great. It is too grainy for music, there is a static sound in the background of everything you are listening to, not a big deal if you are using them for phone conversations, but a definite loser if you are trying to listen to music.

2. It gets more static background noise as the batteries wind down.

Images are in color with more flexibility the Kindle reader on my Mac and I guess that's what I expected, only smaller. If I were only reading fiction, and image quality was not important I would probably keep it rather than go through the hassle of returning it.

As a technical writer I cannot imagine creating such an unfriendly and unwieldy interface. Opened the box less than an hour ago and the "user manual" on the Kindle evidently doesn't have a way to exit the manual or even get back to the the beginning without endlessly pressing the left side of the screen one screen page at a time. Worse yet after after endless "left tapping" I am getting close to the beginning of the manual I am taken forward again to a chapter near the end of the manual. Insane! I just want to get out of the manual or at least access the tool bar and am unable to do so . Supposedly tapping the top of the page allows access to the tool bar but all that does is highlight a word at the top of the page. What's up with this? So far extremely disappointed and frustrated. Nothing should be this difficult. While writing this review the screen changed to the cover and blurb of a book and the Kindle is frozen on that page. By the way, image is dark as is the entire page. It just keeps getting better, folks. Hopefully a restart will remove the kinks and won't be a total waste of money, time and effort. If not this is Kindle is useless and going back. If things improve I will update.

Garmin nüvi 255 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought a new Nuvi 255 for my wife about two years ago. I liked it so much I bought another new one for myself last year. They are great units operationally, but both have exhibited failures. Early this summer, about 18 months of age for the 1st unit and 12 months for the second, they each failed to respond to their respective touchscreens within about a week of each other. I tried the reset button and initiating the touchscreen calibration procedure, but the problem prevailed.
I then connected the first unit to my PC through the USB port and the touchscreen began working afterward. The same cure worked on the second unit. Software glitch I thought.
Well, the older one now exhibits the same failure mode again, and nothing I do helps, including installing the latest firmware update from the Garmin site. I'm worried the other will permanently fail too.
As much as I like the operation of these units, I would not recommend any of the Garmin 2xx family for reliability reasons. I see from internet searches that the problem is not an isolated one. None of the posted "solutions" worked for me. I assume I am not alone. By the way, the frozen unit eventually bypasses the "legal" screen (times out I suppose) and goes into the map navigation mode, although it is still unresponsive to the touch screen.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 255 3.5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Michael Kors Men's & Women's Gen 6 44mm Touchscreen Smart Watch with Alexa Built-In, Fitness Tracker, Sleep Tracker, Heart Rate Monitor, GPS, Music Control, Smartphone Notifications I have used smart watches for a while now and I have seen a steady progression in the technology. This is my first Gen 6 watch. It is a big improvement from what I have used before (beyond just battery life) and so far I am pleased with it.

This is an Android-based smart watch, and it is similar in interface to previous smart watches I have seen and used. If you have used any generation of smart watch before this one the experience is very similar. I won't get too deep into the nuts and bolts of that or the WearOS app.

There are two big areas of improvement I have seen with this new watch. First, the battery life is much better than previous smart watches I have used which is very encouraging. I have a Gen 2 watch that I love but it lasts only about 3 days on a charge, and my Gen 5 is not much better. This one lasts several days before the battery runs out.

The more important improvement to me, though, is the way it doesn't interfere with the Bluetooth in my car. Previous watches messed up my ability to stream to the car's sound system to the point that the sound would sputter and simply die. I did trace it to the watch by powering off the watch completely after which the problem went away and would come back when the watch was powered on. This watch does not interfere at all and my car's Bluetooth works whether the watch is on or not.

This is a stylish watch, a bit more upscale than some of the others I have seen and used. The band is a non-stretch link band that is a little snug but not unworkable.

So far this watch works well for me. I am pleased with the improved battery life and even more happy that it doesn't mess with my car's Bluetooth connectivity.
text_fidelity_b: Michael Kors Men's & Women's Gen 6 44mm Touchscreen Smart Watch with Alexa Built-In, Fitness Tracker, Sleep Tracker, Heart Rate Monitor, GPS, Music Control, Smartphone Notifications

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
LotFancy 7 Inch 16:9 TFT Color LCD Widescreen Car Rear View Monitor Bundle with Remote and Waterproof Camera Many cars on the market come with a rear-view camera that allows for seeing where the vehicle is moving when in reverse. Often the view appears on a dashboard screen. This is handy when parking and maneuvering while the vehicle is backing up. For vehicles that do not have a rear-view camera the alternative is to add on a kit that provides the same functionality. This is my first experience with such a kit and so far I am pleased with it. It does require doing a little work on the vehicle to set it up but the effort is worth it.

The package contains everything needed to set up this camera system. In addition to the camera and the screen, the kit includes the mounting screws for the actual camera as well as all of the wiring to connect everything together and to the power (reverse lights). There is also a mini-remote for interacting with the video screen though this is slightly inconvenient.

I spent a good deal of time reading and rereading the directions and concluded that the instructions could have been better. There are three pieces of documentation in the box; one shows a generalized set of four different configurations for connecting everything together (the fourth diagram on this sheet matches the configuration you want), one is a photocopied image of a wired system and the third is a “User’s Manual” which is one half-sheet of paper with a brief summarization of the product. There really needs to be a better documentation set than this.

If you are not skilled in working with electrical systems, either plan on this taking a good while or have someone you trust install the system. It’s not especially hard to set one of these up, but it does take some patience and a little bit of knowledge of the layout of the car’s wiring. I have worked on car electrical systems in the distant past so I had a vague familiarity, but it still took me a while to have everything set up and working.

Once wired the system is fairly straightforward to use. If it is wired up properly (meaning everything is connected to power on both ends and the two main components can see one another) it works nicely. The image when the camera is feeding to the monitor is bright and reasonably clear; the brightness can be adjusted as needed which helps when using this system at night. Another reviewer commented that he used a different camera connected to this system - while I am personally satisfied with the image quality, it’s reassuring to know that you can use another video camera if desired or necessary.

The addition of the remote will appeal to some, but for me it’s a component that can easily be lost. The menu system on the monitor provides the same functionality as the remote and this is good enough for me.

This is my first experience with rear-view video systems and though it gave me a little trouble setting up it was from lack of good documentation and inexperience, not from being a bad product. Once installed this is a nice and easy-to-use video system. Time will tell how long it works.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy 7 Inch 16:9 TFT Color LCD Widescreen Car Rear View Monitor Bundle with Remote and Waterproof Camera

Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple) [[VIDEOID:e832f455c8dfddb522ae3bbc1ec73698]] Loved the idea of an underwater camera for kids, and this one would have been great if not for the terrible image quality that would only disappoint any except maybe youngest of kids.

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) July 27, 2018 - update. To preface, let me say that my previous Fire tablet was with me for just under 5 years, is still working fine except that it doesn't hold a charge as well as it used to (which is why I went with a new one). This tablet I've had since February so we're talking 5 MONTHS instead of years. As of today, the screen is cracked. Since I don't carry it with me the way I used to carry the previous one, and since the case I have this one in is sturdier than the previous case, and since, to the best of my knowledge, this hasn't been dropped, I'm not pleased. I'm thinking this probably arrived this way, since the crack can only be seen when it is a just the right angle to a bright light. Of course, it won't be covered under the "limited" (that should read VERY limited) warranty, and apparently, I failed to buy the protection plan because I was thinking this was as well built as my previous Kindle. Wrong on all counts. So I will say that it just went down to a 3 star review, partly for the company and not just the Kindle. For all the trouble I had with the books and being able to read books I'd purchased, this was the last thing I expected to happen. If I buy another reader, since I've already figured out I don't like Amazon knowing everything I do through Alexa, it won't be a Kindle.

February 2018 - I just received my new Fire 10 last week. I am moving from my old Fire 8.9, because the battery had decided not to keep a charge, and I was lucky to get 2 hours out of it at one time. Terrible for traveling or using it where there wasn't a plug in available.

I had an unholy amount of problems with the Kindle books on my Fire 10. First once all 1300 books were downloaded, an awful lot of them, at least 20% were unreadable, because of a DRM error. Kindle support did a fine job of straightening that out, although it cost me about 2 hours on chat before it was completed. Then, some books didn't download when they should have so it took what seemed like two days to get them all organized and downloaded. But finally that was straight.

My next problem was with Alexa, whose answer to me is normally, I'm sorry I don't understand. But if the television is on, she apparently can understand the Olympic announcers because she responds to them right away. Because she responds to other voices, once at a restaurant this week, I have to turn her off when we're in public. Obviously, she's far too friendly with strangers. I had heard that this would be a problem, just didn't think it was going to be mine.

I am not a technophile, I can only tell you as an average person using this Fire tablet for all sorts of activities during the day, that it is functional, quick, and works very well with the apps I have loaded. I use my Fire far more that I'll ever use my phone for reading, purchasing, browsing, so I'm very pleased with how it operates. I like the size of the screen, I like the weight. I did not buy Amazon's cover for it, which I'm finding might have been a mistake, but I'll deal with that after the tablet and I have bonded. I can honestly say that when my 8.9 new it didn't work this quickly, so color me pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

FIDO2 Security Key [Folding Design] Thetis Universal Two Factor Authentication USB (Type A) for Multi-Layered Protection (HOTP) in Windows/Linux/Mac OS,Gmail,Facebook,Dropbox,SalesForce,GitHub Thus far this is the only hardware USB key that I have tried that compare to Yubbi. These are about half the price and as you should know if shopping these, you need a minimum of 2. I recommend having at least 3 to 5. If you lose, break, damage or anything causing your device to be innaccessable then in some cases, especially in Crypto exchanges you will not be able to regain access to your assets.

I keep one on me, one in a safe at my house, one in a safety deposit box and another with a trusted friend that has no idea what it goes to. These things are the best protection you can own for logging in to accounts using MFA.

This has the same compatibility as other brands. Worked everywhere it said and more. If you do anything in finance or even online banking or shopping, I would highly recommend looking into these. Not sure why Amazon hasn't added support on here for this type of MFA. Wish they would hurry up and do so. You would think that since they sell them, they would at least add in support for hardware keys to help protect our accounts.

As I said the best security available for a great price. Just make sure to have at least two or you will end up regretting it later.

The nano receiver can be stored in the mouse itself, helpful for on the road travel. The little receiver can also remain in the usb port of your computer. The battery is reputed to last a year and the on/off switch helps you conserve energy.

With its thoughtful design and ease of use, this mouse is ideal for everyday use.

Skullcandy Crusher Wireless Over-Ear Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 40 Hours Battery Life / Extra Bass Tech / Great for Music, School, Workouts, and Gaming - Grey/Tan I got these from Best Buy after reading the glowing and praising reviews, assuming these would compliment my heavily-bassed up music (which is easily more than 3/4 of what I have- I'm literally all about that bass). Honestly, they are terrible when I listen to anything pumped with bass (ie Kesha, Die Antwoord, Zedd, etc). I can't explain it, but something about the sound makes me cringe- it's so distorted and just not good.

HOWEVER, I then tried listening to other genres like rap and rock, and oh my god those songs sound FLAWLESS on these headphones. They just compliment each other so well. It's just so unusual because I thought these headphones were going to bring a whole new positive experience to... well.. bass-y music? Instead it sounds like, well, close your eyes and picture sitting in your car at a red light and hearing one of those annoying people pull up beside you who have a terrible quality radio and speakers and all you hear is distorted and muffled "BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM BOOOOM BOOOOOOOOOOOM"s. That's legit what these Skullcandys sound like and that's only when the bass booster is at MID POINT. I tried putting it all the way up to the highest setting and it sounded like pure garbage.

I'm not an audiophile, BUT I am obsessed with bass and can tell when it's good or not- and Skullcandy definitely dropped the ball on these. I would highly recommend finding another pair if your most listened to genre is heavy dance/electronic/pop/club, BUT these are breathtaking if you listen to genres or any music in general with minimal bass.

Other positives- SO comfortable (I used to have other Skullcandy Crushers and they gave me head aches), sleek (old ones were bulky and imo ugly), VERY easy to use (literally took seconds to pair and figure out), feels durable and like it's made with high quality materials, and had absolutely no connectivity issues.

Overall I'm giving this a 4/5. I'm extremely sad that I'm returning them but they just aren't for me. I hyped myself up so much only to be let down by distortion and overpowering buzzing thumping. I won't lie or give these 1 star because I'm sorry but that's just ridiculous. These headphones are wonderful, just not quite on the money.
text_fidelity_b: Skullcandy Crusher Wireless Over-Ear Bluetooth Headphones for iPhone and Android with Microphone / 40 Hours Battery Life / Extra Bass Tech / Great for Music, School, Workouts, and Gaming - Grey/Tan
